_note: Single source of truth for every label, tooltip, segment, band and metric in the UI. Ranges come from models/model_metadata.json (observed_min/observed_max). Typical values are medians/modes of the saved practice dataset (quick_check_selection.json). Direction hints were verified empirically against the saved model (see quick_check_selection.json 'directions'); hints that contradicted the model were dropped (none needed dropping). Hints describe patterns in practice data, never causes.

Client_Tenure_Months.label: Months with us
Client_Tenure_Months.definition: How many months this client has worked with us.
Client_Tenure_Months.direction_hint: In this demo model, higher values usually go with LOWER risk.

Service_Type.label: Plan
Service_Type.definition: Which plan the client is on.
Service_Type.direction_hint: In this demo model, the Premium (Fiber) plan usually goes with HIGHER risk than Standard (DSL) or no plan.

options.label: Standard (DSL)
options.definition: The standard plan, delivered over phone lines.

options.label: Premium (Fiber)
options.definition: The premium plan, delivered over fiber. Plan names come from the demo dataset.

options.label: No plan
options.definition: The client has no plan with us.

Support_Access.label: Extra support
Support_Access.definition: Whether the client has a dedicated help package.
Support_Access.direction_hint: In this demo model, clients without the extra support package usually show HIGHER risk.

options.label: Yes
options.definition: The client has the extra support package.

options.label: No
options.definition: The client does not have the extra support package.

options.label: Not on a plan
options.definition: The client is not on a plan, so there is no support package. Real value used by the model: "No internet service".

Engagement_Type.label: Contract length
Engagement_Type.definition: How long their agreement runs. Longer contracts are usually harder to leave.
Engagement_Type.direction_hint: In this demo model, month-to-month contracts usually go with HIGHER risk than one- or two-year contracts.

options.label: Month to month
options.definition: The agreement renews every month and can be ended any time.

options.label: One year
options.definition: The agreement runs for one year.

options.label: Two years
options.definition: The agreement runs for two years. Real value used by the model: "Two year".

Monthly_Client_Value.label: Monthly payment
Monthly_Client_Value.definition: What the client pays us each month (demo money units).
Monthly_Client_Value.direction_hint: In this demo model, higher values usually go with HIGHER risk.

Cumulative_Client_Value.label: Total paid so far
Cumulative_Client_Value.definition: Everything the client has paid since joining.
Cumulative_Client_Value.direction_hint: In this demo model, higher values usually go with LOWER risk.

Content_Quality_Score.label: Content quality (0 to 100)
Content_Quality_Score.definition: How good their website content is against Google's quality guidelines. Higher is better.
Content_Quality_Score.direction_hint: In this demo model, higher values usually go with LOWER risk.

Content_Score_Trend_30D.label: Content score change, last 30 days
Content_Score_Trend_30D.definition: How much that score moved. A minus number means it dropped.
Content_Score_Trend_30D.direction_hint: In this demo model, higher values usually go with LOWER risk.

Guideline_Compliance_Score.label: Guideline score (0 to 100)
Guideline_Compliance_Score.definition: How well the content follows Google's Search Quality Guidelines.
Guideline_Compliance_Score.direction_hint: In this demo model, higher values usually go with LOWER risk.

Compliance_Flags.label: Guideline warnings
Compliance_Flags.definition: How many times content was flagged for breaking a guideline.
Compliance_Flags.direction_hint: In this demo model, higher values usually go with HIGHER risk.

Critical_Compliance_Issues.label: Serious guideline issues
Critical_Compliance_Issues.definition: Serious problems (the kind that can hurt Search visibility) still open.
Critical_Compliance_Issues.direction_hint: In this demo model, higher values usually go with HIGHER risk.

Engagement_Score.label: Engagement (0 to 100)
Engagement_Score.definition: One number for how active the client is with us: calls, replies, report views.
Engagement_Score.direction_hint: In this demo model, higher values usually go with LOWER risk.

Monthly_Engagements.label: Contacts per month
Monthly_Engagements.definition: How many times the client replied, joined a call or used the portal in a month.
Monthly_Engagements.direction_hint: In this demo model, higher values usually go with LOWER risk.

Client_Meetings.label: Meetings per month
Client_Meetings.definition: Meetings we had with the client in a month.
Client_Meetings.direction_hint: In this demo model, higher values usually go with LOWER risk.

Report_Views.label: Reports opened
Report_Views.definition: How many times they opened our reports recently.
Report_Views.direction_hint: In this demo model, higher values usually go with LOWER risk.

Response_Rate.label: Reply rate (%)
Response_Rate.definition: Of our messages, what percent the client answered.
Response_Rate.direction_hint: In this demo model, higher values usually go with LOWER risk.

Support_Tickets.label: Help requests
Support_Tickets.direction_hint: In this demo model, higher values usually go with HIGHER risk.

Unresolved_Support_Tickets.label: Open help requests
Unresolved_Support_Tickets.direction_hint: In this demo model, higher values usually go with HIGHER risk.

Avg_Resolution_Time.label: Hours to solve a request
Avg_Resolution_Time.definition: Average hours we take to solve their requests.
Avg_Resolution_Time.direction_hint: In this demo model, higher values usually go with HIGHER risk.

Days_Since_Last_Engagement.label: Days since last contact
Days_Since_Last_Engagement.definition: Days since they last replied, joined a call or opened a report.
Days_Since_Last_Engagement.direction_hint: In this demo model, higher values usually go with HIGHER risk.

Search_Visibility_Change.label: Google visibility change (%)
Search_Visibility_Change.definition: How much more or less their pages show in Google Search versus before. Minus means it dropped.
Search_Visibility_Change.direction_hint: In this demo model, higher values usually go with LOWER risk.

Traffic_Change.label: Website visitors change (%)
Traffic_Change.definition: How much visitors to their site went up or down versus before.
Traffic_Change.direction_hint: In this demo model, higher values usually go with LOWER risk.

Save now.definition: Likely to leave and important to us. Talk to them personally within 7 days.
Save now.example: A client who pays a lot each month, replied to us weeks ago, and has open serious issues.

Automated nudge.definition: Likely to leave, smaller value. Send a helpful email or a short report walkthrough.
Automated nudge.example: A small account on a month-to-month plan that stopped opening reports.

Nurture.definition: Unlikely to leave and important to us. Stay in touch, review every quarter.
Nurture.example: A large account on a two-year contract with steady replies.

Monitor.definition: Unlikely to leave, smaller value. No action now. Keep an eye on them.
Monitor.example: A small account on a one-year contract with regular activity.

Low.definition: The client looks steady. Keep things running as usual.
Low.example: A score of 12 with regular replies and a long contract.

Medium.definition: Some signs to watch. Keep an eye on this client.
Medium.example: A score of 52 after a quiet month.

High.example: A score of 84 with no contact for weeks.

balanced.label: Balanced
balanced.definition: Flags fewer clients, so fewer false alarms.
balanced.example: Best when you have time to check each flagged client.

catch_more.label: Catch more
catch_more.definition: Flags more clients, so you miss fewer leavers, but with more false alarms.
catch_more.example: Best when a missed leaver costs more than an extra phone call.

accuracy.label: Accuracy
accuracy.definition: Of all clients, how often the tool called it right.
accuracy.example: 0.85 means it was right for 85 out of 100 clients.

precision.label: Precision
precision.definition: When it says a client will leave, how often it is right.
precision.example: 0.68 means about 2 in 3 flagged clients really leave.

recall.label: Recall
recall.definition: Of clients who really leave, how many it catches.
recall.example: 0.80 means it catches 8 of every 10 leavers.

f1.label: F1
f1.definition: One score that balances precision and recall.
f1.example: Closer to 1 is better; 0.5 is mediocre.

roc_auc.label: ROC-AUC
roc_auc.definition: How well it tells leaving clients from staying ones. 0.5 is a coin flip, 1 is perfect.
roc_auc.example: 0.91 means it ranks a random leaver above a random stayer 91% of the time.

risk_score.label: Risk score
risk_score.definition: 0 to 100. Higher means more likely to leave. A guide, not a promise.
risk_score.example: 64 means the pattern looks like clients who left in the practice data.
risk_score.direction_hint: Because of how the model was trained, the score is not a true percent of clients who leave.

expected_loss.label: Expected loss
expected_loss.definition: Rough money we could lose = risk score x client value (demo units).
expected_loss.example: Risk 50 on a client worth 1,000 gives about 500.

top_reasons.label: Top reasons
top_reasons.definition: The details that moved this client's score up or down the most.
top_reasons.example: "Days since last contact" with an up arrow means the quiet stretch raised the score.
top_reasons.direction_hint: This shows a pattern in practice data. It does not prove that changing something will keep the client.

practice_data.label: Practice data
practice_data.definition: Made-up data, not real Highspring clients.
practice_data.example: The demo dataset stands in for real client records.

segment.label: Segment
segment.definition: Which of four groups the client falls into, and the matching next step.
segment.example: Save now means: call this client within 7 days.

level.label: Level
level.definition: Low, Medium or High. A short label for the risk score.
level.example: High means clear warning signs; act soon.

confusion_matrix.label: Confusion matrix
confusion_matrix.definition: A small table counting where the tool was right or wrong on the practice test set.
confusion_matrix.example: "Caught 225 leavers, missed 55, raised 106 false alarms, rightly cleared 671 stayers."
